craft_claim: Nostalgia is structurally bittersweet: predominantly positive yet shadowed by absence and loss. A nostalgic tone must hold both valences at once; pure cheer collapses into warmth, pure grief collapses into the elegiac.

supporting_evidence.location: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology 91(5):975-993, content analyses and trigger analyses (Studies 1-4)
supporting_evidence.note: Nostalgic accounts are described in more positive than negative terms yet systematically contain negative feelings, and sad, poignant, lonely events are frequent triggers; the emotion is mixed-valence, not merely pleasant.

supporting_evidence.location: Advances in Experimental Social Psychology 51:189-273, characterization and structure sections
supporting_evidence.note: The chapter's controlling definition: nostalgia is a self-conscious, bittersweet but predominantly positive and fundamentally social emotion arising from fond memories mixed with yearning.

supporting_evidence.location: Emotion 14(4):733-747, ratings of 35 features in 18 countries (N = 1,704)
supporting_evidence.note: Lay prototypes rate nostalgia as more pleasant (happy, warm) than unpleasant (sad, regretful) in every country sampled, while the unpleasant features remain central rather than peripheral: the bitter belongs to the concept.

supporting_evidence.location: History of Psychology 16(3):165-176, abstract and article scope
supporting_evidence.note: Traces the concept from its origins as a medical disease to its contemporary psychological construct - the concept's own history holds the cherished and the pathologized in one word, the bittersweet duality written into the term itself.

Recent review reports nostalgia appraised as positive relative to other self-conscious emotions while insisting it should not be equated with mourning - a predominantly positive emotion that remains distinct from pure sadness.

counterevidence.location: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology 118(2):325-347, Studies 3-5
counterevidence.note: When nostalgia occurs spontaneously in daily life rather than being elicited on request, it covaries negatively with well-being; the 'predominantly positive' profile is partly an artifact of experimental induction, so the writer cannot assume sweetness without the bitter.

scope: Core shape of the tone: valence structure of nostalgic recollection; feeds card sections on core shape and boundaries.
exceptions: Registers of pure fondness without absence belong to tone-warm; registers of present loss without the fond, idealized distance belong to tone-elegiac.
